title: Flaky test-ordering failure in python tests/coap/test_edhoc_responder.py
description: Running the full file fails one timing/state-dependent test, but each test passes in isolation; which test fails varies between runs (observed test_close_during_completion_cancels_publication_without_success and test_expiry_before_m3_never_reaches_blocked_put failing on different runs, both passing alone). Shared mutable state (module/class-level responder or publication state, or real time.time()-based expiry racing) leaks between tests. Found on beads-worker-4 while validating 7xyr (unrelated changes; failure reproduces with changes stashed). Fix: isolate per-test state or freeze time.
close_reason: Root cause was NOT shared test state or timing: 100% of observed failures (31 across 25 runs) were ValueError 'signature verification failed' at edhoc.py:508 in process_message_2. Real product bug: _validate_connection_id decoded CBOR compact-integer CIDs with value+256 (-1 -> 0xFF) instead of 0x1F-value (-1 -> 0x20), breaking the RFC 9528 3.3.2 round-trip for CID bytes 0x20-0x37. Responder picks c_r=os.urandom(1), so ~9.4% of handshakes rebuilt a wrong context_2/MAC_2 on the initiator side and rejected the responder's valid Signature_2 - order-dependent flakiness was a symptom (random c_r), not cause. Fix: edhoc.py:227 decode negative compact ints as 0x1F-value. Tests added in tests/crypto/test_edhoc.py: exhaustive 256-byte CID roundtrip with pinned RFC wire forms (external oracle), deterministic handshake regression with c_r=b'0x21'. Verification: 0/30 suite runs fail (was 20/25), 4000-handshake stress clean, tests/crypto + tests/coap/test_edhoc_responder.py 798 passed. 3x codereview delegated to reviewer model (kimi-k3, plan agent): correctness PASS, security PASS (no CID-collision, C_R==C_I bypass, or cross-session confusion), edge-cases PASS - zero findings. Note: 5 pre-existing failures in tests/coap/ (tunnel_auth_resource, lci_identity_vectors) are unrelated migration gaps, verified failing with the fix stashed; tunnel_auth covered by lptm/gla0/xf1v/7jcp, lci corpus filed as 0qcc.
